title: Java News Roundup: JobRunr 9, OpenXava 8, Quarkus, LangChain4j, JNoSQL, Introducing Lathe
gist: Weekly Java roundup: JEP 544 AOT compilation targeted for JDK 28, a firm Jakarta EE 12 schedule (Core Dec 1, Web Mar 31, Platform May 15), and a steady stream of AI-agent tooling (LangChain4j decision models, Google ADK, Lathe with an MCP server).

themes.theme: Jakarta EE 12 timeline and NoSQL/AI push

insights.claim: Jakarta EE 12 is firmed up as a staged rollout: Core Profile December 1, Web Profile March 31, full Platform May 15, set after the steering committee asked for a clearer timeline.
insights.speaker: Ivar Grimstad
insights.so_what: Gives enterprise Java shops dated targets for planning upgrades; the platform lands about 5-6 months after Core.

insights.claim: Jakarta EE's developer advocate argues Jakarta NoSQL belongs in the Jakarta EE 12 Web Profile because standardized NoSQL access, especially vector database support for RAG, matters when integrating AI into enterprise applications.
insights.speaker: Ivar Grimstad
insights.so_what: Signals the standards body is trying to make AI/RAG data access a first-class enterprise Java concern.
insights.quote: Particularly, support for vector databases for RAG is something that will be very useful.

insights.claim: A vote is ongoing to add Jakarta Authorization to the Jakarta EE Web Profile, grouped with the other security specifications.
insights.speaker: Ivar Grimstad
insights.so_what: Profile scope is still being decided, so Web Profile content could shift.

insights.claim: Eclipse JNoSQL, the Jakarta NoSQL implementation, was promoted from incubating to a full EE4J project; it has been an Eclipse project since 2017 and in GlassFish since Jakarta EE 11 via Jakarta Data support.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Maturity milestone that supports the case for standardizing NoSQL in Jakarta EE.

insights.claim: Eclipse JNoSQL 1.19.0 adds ScyllaDB support and updates drivers for Neo4J 6.3.0, InfluxDB 1.11.1, DynamoDB 2.55.7 and MongoDB 5.13.0.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Shows the multi-database breadth of the Java NoSQL abstraction layer.

insights.claim: JEP 544, Ahead-of-Time Code Compilation, was moved to Targeted for JDK 28, aiming to give HotSpot applications optimized native code at startup so they reach and sustain peak performance sooner.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Would cut JVM warmup cost, narrowing Java's gap with native-image and serverless-oriented runtimes.

insights.claim: JDK 28 early-access Build 18 shipped, with fixes over Build 17.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: JDK 28 is in routine pre-release iteration.

themes.theme: Java frameworks and job processing releases

insights.claim: JobRunr 9.0.0 reached GA with a Gantt-style job history chart showing a row per state and per durable step, support for Micronaut 5 and Quarkus 3.40, and a warning for oversized serialized jobs.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Durable-step execution is a growing feature in Java background-job tooling.

insights.claim: OpenXava 8.0.0 is now built on Spring Boot and supports some Jakarta EE 11 specifications, with a more modern look and feel.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Low-code Java frameworks continue to consolidate onto Spring Boot.

insights.claim: Micronaut 5.2.0 and 5.2.1 add experimental Micronaut for Python, which processes Python source at compile time, plus a Jakarta EL module.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: A JVM framework is experimenting with compile-time processing of Python, an unusual cross-language move.

insights.claim: Quarkus 3.34.0 shipped with launcher hardening and removal of a spurious RESTEasy Reactive Jackson warning, alongside the 3.40.0 and 3.40.1 releases.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Minor maintenance releases; steady cadence with no major shift.

themes.theme: AI agent tooling in the Java ecosystem

insights.claim: LangChain4j 1.21.0 introduces experimental decision models, a new API with DecisionModel, DecisionServices, RoutingChatModel and DecisionRouterPlanner.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Java LLM frameworks are moving toward routing and planning abstractions for agents.

insights.claim: Google's ADK for Java 1.11.0 adds thread-safe Session event methods (immutableEvents, addEvent, addEvents) and deprecates events(), plus rewind compatibility with ADK for Kotlin.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Google is keeping Java and Kotlin agent SDKs aligned and hardening concurrency for production agents.

insights.claim: ADK for Kotlin 1.3.0 adds an @ExperimentalLiveApi annotation marking a live bidirectional streaming API.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Real-time streaming agent interaction is arriving in Google's JVM SDKs, still experimental.

insights.claim: Lathe, a new Java language server by Alexey Gavrilov of Telenor Linx, derives its model from a Maven build to avoid classpath configuration and ships both a Neovim client and an MCP server for AI coding agents.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: MCP servers are becoming a default deliverable even for developer tools like language servers, serving AI coding agents.
insights.quote: Lathe ships with a Neovim client and an MCP server for AI coding agents.

insights.claim: Lathe is at version 0.1.14, so it is early-stage and adoption is unproven.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Early-stage tool; watch for traction among AI-agent-driven Java workflows.
